{{Overwatch}}: 2021-04-04 }} '''Team Falcons''' (formerly known as '''Falcons Esport''') is a [[:category:Saudi Arabia|Saudi Arabian]] esports organization. ==History== Team Falcons entered ''Overwatch'' in 2021 by announcing their roster for [[Saudi_eLeagues/2021/Season_1|Saudi eLeagues 2021 Season 1]], which they narrowly won, spearheaded by MVP [[Fuki]]. In the next three eLeagues tournaments, Falcons ended second place, each time losing to [[01 Esports]] (the future [[Twisted Minds]] core). The organization also hosted a separate team for [[Contenders]], known as [[Falcons Esport EU]], which ran throughout 2021 and won 3 of the 4 tournaments that year. They released both EMEA rosters in 2022. ===OWCS 2024=== Team Falcons reentered ''Overwatch'' for OWCS 2024 with the signing of free-agent team "Hamster". The roster consisted of ex-2023 [[Atlanta Reign]] players [[Stalk3r]], [[Fielder]] and [[ChiYo]] along other [[OWL]] stars [[Proper]], [[Hanbin]] and [[Fearless]]. The latter was not retained but replaced with [[Smurf]], and [[SirMajed]], the only non-Korean player in the tournament, was added as well. This roster was the most decorated team in the world, its players boasting 5 [[OWL]] championships and numerous other accolades, making them the most awaited team for the start of OWCS. During [[Overwatch_Champions_Series/2024/Asia/Stage_1/Korea|Korea Stage 1]], Falcons beat WAC (later to be signed to [[Crazy Raccoon]]) to win the regional trophy, however, they fell to CR in the [[Overwatch_Champions_Series/2024/Asia/Stage_1/Main_Event|Asia Stage 1]] finals the month after. This rivalry continuted at the [[Overwatch_Champions_Series/2024/Major|Dallas Major]] global tournament, where Falcons beat CR in the Winner's Final but then lost to them in the Grand Final, finishing 2nd overall. Team Falcons qualified to the [[Esports_World_Cup/2024|Esports World Cup]] in Riyadh with their OWCS placement. At the event, an upset loss to [[LGD.OA]] (the [[Team China]] 2023 roster) gave them the second seed in their group behind [[Twisted Minds]]. This eventually resulted in them being placed in the same side of the Single Elimination bracket as Crazy Raccoon, thus the Dallas Major finals could not be repeated. The teams met in the Semifinal, where a 1-4 defeat gave this Falcons roster their lowest placement thus far. Ahead of [[Overwatch_Champions_Series/2024/Asia/Stage_2/Korea|OWCS 2024 Korea Stage 2]], Falcons signed [[Happy]], quashing speculation about his retirement. Because Happy is a hitscan player, the signing could allow [[Proper]] to play more flex/projectile DPS heroes such as Genji. The team was considered to be weaker than expected in the Regular Season,{{citation needed}} however, they upset their rivals and reigning champions [[Crazy Raccoon]] in the semifinals. They defeated [[ZETA DIVISION]] 4-1 in the Grand Final, winning their second Korean title. At [[Overwatch_Champions_Series/2024/Asia/Stage_2/Main_Event|Asia Stage 2]], they once again went up against their rival CR and beat them in a legendary 4-3 series, snatching the Asia champions title and heading to the final global event as Korea's 1st seed. In the [[Overwatch_Champions_Series/2024/Finals|World Finals]] in Stockholm, Falcons found huge success on the ultimate-centric Mauga-Juno-Brigitte composition that dominated the meta. They swept through the bracket, dropping only two maps and once again defeating their arch-nemesis Crazy Raccoon to win the championship. [[Stalk3r]] was named the tournament MVP for his exceptional Echo play. ===OWCS 2025=== Team Falcons started their 2025 run as the defending OWCS World Champions and remained with the original Hamster core, following the retirements of [[Happy]] and [[Smurf]]. After a somewhat unimpressive showing in [[Overwatch_Champions_Series/2025/Asia/Stage_1/Korea|Korea Stage 1]] regular season, they also fell 0-4 to [[Crazy Raccoon]] in playoffs semifinals. However, Falcons swept through [[Overwatch_Champions_Series/2025/Asia/Stage_1|Asia Stage 1]] and despite losing 0-4 to CR in upper finals, they reversed the result by winning the rematch Grand Final 4-2, claiming the title and heading to the first global tournament of the year as Korea's 1st seed. At [[Overwatch_Champions_Series/2025/Champions_Clash|Champions Clash]], they advanced through the upper bracket with a notably close 3-2 series against [[Once Again]], while Crazy Raccoon went through the lower bracket. Falcons ultimately lost 2-4 against CR in the Grand Final. Ahead of the second stage, Falcons announced the signing of [[Overwatch_League/2023|2023 OWL]] stars [[MER1T]] and [[Someone]], who had been inactive in Stage 1. Now cumulating 10 championships accross their players, Team Falcons were said to have become truly unbeatable. This was quickly disproven as [[Overwatch_Champions_Series/2025/Asia/Stage_2/Korea|Korea Stage 2]] started and they successively lost 1-3 to [[ZETA DIVISION]], 0-3 to [[All Gamers Global]], benched Proper halfway, finished 5th in regular season and got knocked out in playoffs quarterfinals by [[Crazy Raccoon]]. Falcons ended Stage 2 at the 5th-6th place, having to rely on the [[Overwatch_Champions_Series/2025/Midseason_Championship/LCQ|Last Chance Qualifiers]] for a spot at the global tournament. This result generated a lot of discussions about the integration of [[MER1T]] and [[SOMEONE]], especially after the statement put out by head coach [[NineK]] about a "collective rebuilding phase"{{cite web|url=https://x.com/NineK_OW/status/1926152910330626260|title=@NineK_OW|author=[[NineK]]|date=2024-05-24}} which had led to the benching of Proper. From the LCQ onward, Falcons re-integrated Proper in place of Stalk3r and gained back their form, beating [[ZETA DIVISION]] 3-0 in the finals and qualifying for the global tournament. At the [[Overwatch_Champions_Series/2025/Midseason_Championship|Midseason Championship]], they did not drop a series, defeated [[Geekay Esports]] 3-2 and [[T1]] 3-1 in playoffs while rivals Crazy Raccoon had been eliminated early in quarterfinals, and ended on a clean 4-0 sweep against [[Al Qadsiah]] in the Grand Final. Their comeback from the bottom was topped with [[Proper]] being selected as Tournament MVP. In the off-season, Falcons shocked again by not registering [[Stalk3r]] which would make them unable to field him for the remainder of the year. During [[Overwatch_Champions_Series/2025/Asia/Stage_3/Korea|Korea Stage 3]], Falcons swept through the regular season but got upset 2-4 by [[WAE]] in playoffs quarterfinals, once again concluding regionals at the 5th-6th place. In a repeat scenario of Stage 2, Falcons rised from the bottom to qualify for LAN at [[Overwatch_Champions_Series/2025/Asia/Stage_3/Championship/Korea|Korea Road to World Finals]] by successively beating [[ONSIDE GAMING]], [[ZETA DIVISION]], [[Crazy Raccoon]] and [[T1]]. They finally met CR in finals but bowed 3-4 to a reverse sweep and qualified as Korea's 2nd seed. At [[Overwatch_Champions_Series/2025/World_Finals|World Finals]] in Stockholm, they fell out of the upper bracket in semifinals to an allmighty [[Twisted Minds]], then went on to be eliminated for good by CR in lower semifinals, thus finishing the year as only the 4th best team in the world this time. ===OWCS 2026=== Team Falcons released both their founding star DPS players [[Proper]] (headed to [[ZETA DIVISION]]) and [[Stalk3r]] (headed to [[Crazy Raccoon]]), recruiting [[Checkmate]] in their place and also welcoming back their 2024 coach [[Junkbuck]]. They kicked off the year with a rather satisfying 3rd-4rd place finish at the [[Overwatch_Champions_Series/2026/Stage_1/Pre-Season_Bootcamp|Pre-Season Bootcamp]], after playing narrow 2-3 series against [[Weibo Gaming]] and their rivals [[Crazy Raccoon]]. In [[Overwatch_Champions_Series/2025/Asia/Stage_1/Korea|Korea Stage 1]], despite repeated losses against [[Crazy Raccoon]] and new powerhouse [[ZETA DIVISION]], Falcons advanced to the stage's Grand Final after beating CR 4-1 in playoffs semifinals. They ultimately failed to take the crown to an unbeatable ZETA and finished runner-ups of the region. But at [[Overwatch_Champions_Series/2025/Asia/Stage_1|Asia Stage 1]] where they competed for the qualification to [[Overwatch_Champions_Series/2026/Champions_Clash|Champions Clash]], a first-of-its-kind scenario occured during the group stage where [[VARREL]]'s upset 2-1 win against CR caused Falcons to finish 3rd place of their group. This prevented Falcons from advancing to playoffs, thus failing to qualify for a major for the first time since OWCS started. Falcons added a third DPS to their roster in the off-season by signing rookie [[SP1NT]], but kept struggling in [[Overwatch_Champions_Series/2025/Asia/Stage_2/Korea|Korea Stage 2]]. They were still unable to beat the other two top dogs [[Crazy Raccoon]] and [[ZETA DIVISION]], and as hitscan [[MER1T]] had to sit out due to an injury, Falcons lost to [[T1]] for the first time during seeding deciders and went on to finish the stage at the 5-6th place after losing 2-4 to [[ZANSIDE GAMING]] in the playoffs quarterfinals. Still, Falcons travelled to the [[Overwatch_Champions_Series/2026/Midseason_Championship|Midseason Championship]] thanks to the EWC Title Defender program. During the group stage, they swept NA's [[Dallas Fuel]] 2-0, but dropped to the lower bracket after losing 1-2 to China's [[Weibo Gaming]] and were knocked out the tournament after a new 0-2 loss against a revigorated [[T1]].
